attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No Yang-Mills estimate yet supplies uniform H,K and o(eta^2) for reflected Wilson hairpin products in the locked algebra.
steps: Normalize the finite Wilson block so diagonal entries are one; the collar quotient then tends to E=11^*.
Decompose C^n=Ce plus 1^perp. Positivity of q_delta is equivalent to positivity of the Schur complement because the e-block is n+O(eta).
Expanding the Schur complement gives eta PHP plus eta^2 P(K-n^{-1}Hee^*H)P; one-body diagonal congruences vanish under P.
If PHP has a negative vector, or the corrected K-form is negative on ker(PHP), then q_delta has a negative quadratic form for small collars.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The finite-matrix argument is valid, but the analytic boundary OPE computation and same-theory identification of Bh_delta are missing.

assumptions: Bh_delta has nonzero entries and q_delta is Hermitian with diagonal one.
q_delta=E+eta_delta H+eta_delta^2 K+o(eta_delta^2) uniformly for the finite block, with H,K Hermitian.
q_delta>=0 is equivalent to OS positivity of the intended Schur-preimage matrix for this block.
The collar RG convergence is valid for all reflected Wilson products used in H and K.
definitions: source object: diagonal-normalized collar quotient matrices q_delta=Nh_delta oslash Bh_delta from regulated reflected Wilson OS blocks.
target object: finite OS quadratic forms of the intended continuum Schwinger functions on the same Wilson observables.
controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions via Schur-preimage positivity after collar collapse.
same-theory condition: remove only the locked boundary Gram factor; add no boundary observable, counterterm, or changed Wilson-loop renormalization.

equations.valid_when: valid when the boundary Wilson OPE gives a uniform second-order collar expansion.

equations.label: Schur complement at vacuum direction
equations.valid_when: valid for e=n^{-1/2}{\bf1}, P=I-ee^*, after eliminating the large rank-one OS direction.

equations.label: second-order falsifier
equations.valid_when: valid for small eta_delta if the remainder is uniform on the chosen finite Wilson block.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find a locked reflected Wilson block whose computed H,K violate the first gate or the Schur-corrected second gate.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Turns Wilson boundary OPE data into a finite same-theory OS positivity test beyond closed-cone formalism.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For a locked finite reflected Wilson hairpin block with a uniform second-order collar quotient expansion near the rank-one matrix, OS positivity of the same-theory target has a valid tangent test: PHP>=0 and a Schur-corrected K-form is nonnegative on ker(PHP).

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if the RG topology cannot even define the quotient expansion q_delta for reflected Wilson products.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if a dense Wilson core satisfies PHP>=0 and the Schur-corrected second gate for all finite blocks.
control_decision.reason: The branch now has a compact finite-matrix bridge and a precise analytic target: compute H,K with uniform remainders for locked reflected Wilson hairpins.

dependency_updates.description: Fixed-collar closed-cone transfer remains formal; the active bridge is now Schur-preimage positivity of Wilson collar quotients.
Must control reflected Wilson quotient expansions through second order with uniform remainders.
The Wilson core must be stable under collar deformation and boundary Gram normalization without adding boundary fields.

falsifiers: first-order falsifier: a vector v in 1^perp with v^*PHPv<0 for a computed Wilson hairpin block.
second-order falsifier: PHP>=0 but u in ker(PHP) makes u^*P(K-n^{-1}Hee^*H)Pu<0.
The collar OPE remainder is not uniform, so the tangent sign does not control actual q_delta for small cutoff.
Bh_delta requires a boundary counterterm or changed Wilson renormalization, violating the same-theory condition.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 223 made the Wilson obstruction a normalization-safe tangent-cone lemma. The correction -n^{-1}PHee^*HP is forced by the rank-one vacuum direction, so a negative corrected K-form is a genuine mixed boundary falsifier, not a one-body renormalization artifact.
